rv.q: The friction between their personalities produces terrific chemistry, and the smart book guarantees that, while their early exchanges are abrasive, they’re also genuinely witty.
That's the entertaining idea behind the sassy new musical comedy, "First Date."
This small musical about a blind date gone right is surprisingly sweet and often funny, with a terrific performance by Zachary Levi.
This modest, unassuming tuner is a definite crowd-pleaser.
You’ll never see a bad show there, or even a fair one.

Despite a little overeagerness, First Date isn't a bad night out (provided you don't expect deep engagement). If ever there were the platonic ideal of a Broadway summer engagement, this is it: no serious competition, low expectations, emerging talent.
I have been harsh on this modest musical, efficiently if facelessly directed by Bill Berry, so I should underscore that Mr. Levi and Ms. Rodriguez are both appealing performers.
The fun time they provide is definitely deserving of a goodnight kiss.
Austin Winsberg's slapstick book makes hash of every dating cliche we've heard...The breezy if plain score is by young composers Alan Zachary and Michael Weiner, who've written for Disney...
Levi and Rodriguez both sing well, and establish a very winning rapport.

First Date is a pleasant enough diversion that makes the most of its modest ambitions. The show's best asset is its appealing leads, Zachary Levi and Krysta Rodriguez, who have an easy chemistry that makes you root for their characters.
But Levi and Rodriguez are so refreshingly honest in their interplay, we wind up rooting for them to get together despite the hokey world they inhabit.
“First Date” — a new Broadway musical about, you guessed it, a first date — is just as generic, pedestrian, bare and altogether uninteresting as the title implies that it will be.
Well, yes — and so is just about everything else in this dopey midsummer entry, which opened Thursday at the Longacre Theatre.
All fine, but not enough to recommend the show.

cn.t: Critics are split on this modest musical about a blind date: some find it cute and charming with winning performances from Levi and Rodriguez, while others dismiss it as generic, sitcom-lite material unworthy of Broadway.
